hook.line: Three tips to use Claude Code better than 99% of people.
hook.visual: Man at a laptop holds up three fingers; a box at top types out '3 TIPS FOR CLAUDE CODE'; the Claude logo fades onto the laptop lid as he says the name.

beats.what: Three fingers up, title typed on, Claude logo appears on the laptop lid
Tip 1 headline typed into the top box: 'CREATE CLAUDE.MD'
Cut to a full-screen CLAUDE.md file with his face in a circle bubble
Scroll to the documentation-links section of the file as he explains
Cut back to him; tip 2 'SUB-CLAUDE.MD' typed into the top box
Split: an animated file-tree diagram on top, him below
Diagram highlights the root and sub CLAUDE.md merging into context
Cut back to him for tip 3: evolve the file over time
Cut to a blurred file with the 'Documentation Updates' rule in focus above him

why_it_works: 'Better than 99% of people' plus three raised fingers sets status and length in under 3 s
Each tip gets its own typed headline in the same top box, so the structure is visible without listening
A cut to the real file or a diagram lands on each tip, so every claim is shown, not just told
45 s at 4.2 words/s: dense, no filler, easy to rewatch
weaknesses: Ends abruptly mid-sentence with no CTA in the video (the caption carries the link-in-bio ask)
The code file frames are tiny text; most viewers will not read them
for_robert: Use one fixed headline box that types each tip's name as he says it; Fred could be the one typing it or tapping it on.
